title: Wagon advertisements and battles between bands
summary: Ridgley recalls advertising wagons where two or three bands met on corners and took turns, and players had to think up things to do.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: It was a, sometimes you know, I don't know, you're just like anything else, you just, it's just off, it looks like you just can't get yourself together. Done the game, you're just to, let's get together and just tear them things open like that. The time they would get out on those wagon advertisements and trucking, we used to do all the time like that. But you had to be a good figure. You had to put in something. Because it wouldn't look for you just to come down and play that tune like it was written or nothing like that. Other people, you'd come along there cutting it up and everybody's cutting it up and tearing your pieces. You had to do it too. So we used to play those wagon advertisements all day and we used to meet on the corner, sometimes two, three bands. And the guys would buy drinks, the fellas liked to drink. We had a battle royale right there. Take turns, the bands would take turns. You'd play your friend and group for you, but you had to be good. You had to think, I used to think sometime how we got all that stuff together.
It was a miracle how you did it. All the fellas down there and they came out so good in it. It's changed the whole world of music, you know, that faking stuff.
